def test_summary_not_shared_between_tenants_bill_2291(svc):
    # BILL-2291: B read right after A, no write in between, same period.
    a = svc.get_invoice_summary("acme", "2024-05")
    b = svc.get_invoice_summary("globex", "2024-05")
    assert a["total_cents"] == 12_500
    assert b["total_cents"] == 99_900


def test_customer_not_shared_between_tenants(svc):
    assert svc.get_customer("acme", "c-1")["name"] == "Acme Buyer"
    assert svc.get_customer("globex", "c-1")["name"] == "Globex Buyer"
EOF

import re
p='src/cache.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''def make_key(op, entity_id):
    # Build the cache key from the operation name and the entity id
    return f"{op}:{entity_id}"''','''def make_key(tenant_id, op, entity_id):
    # The tenant must be part of the key: the cache may be shared across
    # tenants, and entity ids / periods are not unique across tenants (BILL-2291).
    return f"{tenant_id}:{op}:{entity_id}"''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/service.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''# make_key leaves the tenant out of the key on purpose: each tenant is pinned to its
# own worker pool with its own Cache instance (BILL-1874), so it would be redundant.
''','''# Cache keys are tenant-scoped. Don't rely on per-tenant worker pools (BILL-1874)
# for isolation: in prod a Cache instance can serve several tenants (BILL-2291).
''')
s=s.replace('key = make_key(op, entity_id)','key = make_key(tenant_id, op, entity_id)')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
